item.title: KeNHA Announces Two-Week Closure of Major Highway
item.description: Motorists have been advised to adhere to the proposed traffic plan and cooperate with police and traffic marshals.

item.title: DCI Nabs Masterminds Behind Fake 2025 KCSE Result Slips
item.description: According to the DCI, the teacher used social media platforms to target desperate parents and candidates, promising them 'upgraded' KCSE result slips.

item.title: DCI Intercepts Multi-Million Consignment Headed to Nakuru
item.description: The total amount of the intercepted drugs is valued at around KSh 11,610,000 according to the detectives.

item.title: Gov’t Moves to Protect Small-Scale Farmers From Financial Exploitation
item.description: Farmers have continued to complain against the agency, with primary concerns being exploitation, favoritism, and management opacity.

item.title: NTSA Issues Notice to Some Aspiring Vehicle Owners
item.description: The authority has urged individuals to visit the NTSA portal, upload several documents, and wait for seven days for feedback.

item.title: Gachagua Breaks Silence on Cleophas Malala’s Mysterious Absence
item.description: Malala has maintained a low profile, notably missing key engagements that Gachagua has been involved in recently.

item.title: Police Officer Arrested After Shooting Man
item.description: According to Independent Policing Authority (IPOA), the officer shot the man following brief confrontation as he was on patrol.

item.title: Omtatah Clarifies His Petition on HIV Treatment Funding
item.description: According to the Busia Senator, proper legal safeguards protect patients by preventing misuse, diversion, or exploitation of health systems, sensitive patient data, and funds.

item.title: Sakaja Announces Free Business Licenses for Some Nairobi Youth
item.description: The governor argued that his decision to waive the fees followed repeated complaints from young entrepreneurs starting businesses in the city.

item.title: NTSA Suspends 4 Matatu SACCOs
item.description: NTSA said that the four Saccos failed to adhere to road safety regulations that were set during the 2025 festive season.
